facts.raw_span: severe bilateral pneumonia
recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history was reported
blurred vision and redness in her right eye
temporary (8-day) pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD
Relative afferent pupil defect
Central scotoma
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR
Cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts (normal results)
Fluorescein Angiography (Day 30): Mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage

concepts.why: The patient was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia and had a positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2.
The patient developed blurred vision and redness in her right eye, with a relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma, consistent with optic neuritis.
The patient had fluorescein angiography showing mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage, consistent with retinal vasculitis.
The patient was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia.
The patient had a positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 and was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia.
It explains the combination of decreased visual acuity, central scotoma, and normal cranial MRI results.

rationales.F01: Severe bilateral pneumonia is more common in COVID-19 and viral pneumonia.
rationales.F04: Blurred vision and redness in one eye are symptoms of optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis.
rationales.F06: Best-corrected visual acuity of +2 logMAR indicates severe visual impairment, consistent with optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis.
rationales.F09: Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 is a strong indicator of COVID-19.
rationales.F12: Fluorescein Angiography showing mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage is consistent with optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of blurred vision, redness, and pain in the right eye, along with specific findings like relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and optic nerve atrophy, strongly support optic neuritis, which is a more specific diagnosis than the broader COVID-19, despite the positive SARS-CoV-2 test.
